cards.title: NYU Researchers Identify Biomarkers in Human Milk Linking Nutrition to Infant Growth
cards.content: Researchers at NYU Grossman School of Medicine identified seven candidate biomarkers in human milk that are associated with maternal nutritional status, infant growth, and biological processes within the mammary gland. The biomarkers, including four short-chain acylcarnitines, were found by analyzing 1,543 milk samples from three geographically and nutritionally diverse cohorts. The study found that the biomarkers can provide a window into the biology of milk production and how it connects with maternal nutrition and infant growth.
